title: FCC: Ban on Foreign-Made Robots Includes Robot Vacuums
excerpt: It's bad news for Chinese robot vacuum manufacturers like Roborock, Ecovacs, and Dreame, which dominate the market. The ban will also ensnare robot lawn mowers.
content_html:
The US ban on foreign-made advanced robotic devices targets more than just futuristic humanoid machines. It also reaches into people’s homes by covering robot vacuums, too. 

The Federal Communications Commission today confirmed to PCMag that the newly announced ban, which stems from a White House order, covers both robot vacuums and robot lawn mowers. 

In announcing the ban, the FCC specifically named "mobile robots, such as humanoids and quadrupeds." However, an FAQ says the agency defines advanced robotic devices as "a mechanical mobile device [that] is capable of locomotion, obstacle avoidance, navigation, or movement on the ground," which sounds a lot like robot vacuums.

It also covers devices that weigh over 4.4 pounds in total, including ground or docking stations. Many robot vacuums are well over 5 or 10 pounds, especially when the dock is included. The Ecovacs Deebot X8 Pro Omni, a PCMag Editors’ Choice, comes in at 11.7 pounds.

(Credit: FCC.gov)

Other requirements include a sensor capable of perceiving its surroundings, wireless connectivity, and local software installed — all features that robot vacuums have. The FAQ only explicitly excludes drones, connected vehicles, unmanned underwater craft, along with robot arms and assistive devices, from the ban.

It’s bad news for Chinese robot vacuum manufacturers. According to research firm IDC, the top five last year were all Chinese companies, with Roborock, Ecovacs, and Dreame leading the sector. 

(Credit: IDC)

However, the US ban only covers new advanced robot models, not existing products that have already received FCC equipment authorization for sale in the US. The "action does not impact a consumer’s continued use of devices they previously acquired," the FCC says. "Nor does it prevent retailers from continuing to sell, import, or market relevant models approved previously.”

A separate FCC order also indicates that any existing robot vacuums already authorized "may continue to receive software and firmware updates that mitigate harm to US consumers at least until January 1, 2029." The cutoff time also applies to foreign-made drones and Wi-Fi routers, but it's possible the FCC could extend it through a future rulemaking.

Still, the ban threatens to block any new Chinese robot vacuums from reaching the US. Through the FCC, a company can apply to receive an exemption from the ban. But it’ll be up to the Defense Department or the Department of Homeland Security to sign off on the exemption, and it's unclear whether the Trump administration is willing to do so. The White House has enforced similar bans on foreign-made drones and Wi-Fi routers, and so far, no exemption has been granted to a major Chinese vendor.

Recommended by Our Editors

In deciding to ban the foreign-made robots, the White House cited the threat of the US becoming over-reliant on foreign suppliers for robot components and technologies. The same reliance could create a way for a foreign entity to "disrupt or degrade the supply chains at a time of their choosing.” Another concern is that spying may occur through the robots' sensors.

“Given this evidence, the US government has a clear and compelling national security concern that foreign-produced advanced robotic devices could be weaponized to directly harm US national security and US persons,” the FCC says.

The document also cites a few news articles about US robotics relying on Chinese components and an alleged backdoor found preinstalled in a robot dog product from Unitree.

About Our Expert

Michael Kan

Principal Reporter

Experience

I've been a journalist for over 15 years. I got my start as a schools and cities reporter in Kansas City and joined PCMag in 2017, where I cover satellite internet services, cybersecurity, PC hardware, and more. I'm currently based in San Francisco, but previously spent over five years in China, covering the country's technology sector.

Since 2020, I've covered the launch and explosive growth of SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet service, writing 600+ stories on availability and feature launches, but also the regulatory battles over the expansion of satellite constellations, fights with rival providers like AST SpaceMobile and Amazon, and the effort to expand into satellite-based mobile service. I've combed through FCC filings for the latest news and driven to remote corners of California to test Starlink's cellular service.

I also cover cyber threats, from ransomware gangs to the emergence of AI-based malware. In 2024 and 2025, the FTC forced Avast to pay consumers $16.5 million for secretly harvesting and selling their personal information to third-party clients, as revealed in my joint investigation with Motherboard.

I also cover the PC graphics card market. Pandemic-era shortages led me to camp out in front of a Best Buy to get an RTX 3000. I'm now following how the AI-driven memory shortage is impacting the entire consumer electronics market. I'm always eager to learn more, so please jump in the comments with feedback and send me tips.

美国联邦通信委员会今天向 PCMag 证实，新宣布的禁令源自白宫命令，涵盖机器人吸尘器和机器人割草机。

FCC在宣布禁令时特别点名“移动机器人，例如类人机器人和四足机器人”。 然而，常见问题解答称，该机构将先进机器人设备定义为“一种能够移动、避障、导航或在地面上移动的机械移动设备”，这听起来很像机器人吸尘器。

这对于中国扫地机器人制造商来说是个坏消息。 根据研究公司 IDC 的数据，去年排名前五的都是中国公司，其中石头科技、科沃斯和梦想领跑。

（来源：IDC）

不过，美国的禁令仅涵盖新型先进机器人型号，不适用于已获得 FCC 设备授权在美国销售的现有产品。 FCC 表示，“这一行动不会影响消费者继续使用他们之前购买的设备”。 “这也不妨碍零售商继续销售、进口或营销之前批准的相关型号。”

FCC 的另一项命令还表明，任何已获得授权的现有机器人吸尘器“至少在 2029 年 1 月 1 日之前可能会继续接收软件和固件更新，以减轻对美国消费者的伤害”。 该截止时间也适用于外国制造的无人机和 Wi-Fi 路由器，但 FCC 可能会通过未来的规则制定来延长该时间。

尽管如此，该禁令仍有可能阻止任何新的中国机器人吸尘器进入美国。 通过 FCC，公司可以申请获得禁令豁免。 但豁免将由国防部或国土安全部签署，目前尚不清楚特朗普政府是否愿意这样做。 白宫对外国制造的无人机和 Wi-Fi 路由器也实施了类似的禁令，到目前为止，还没有一家主要的中国供应商获得豁免。

我们的编辑推荐

在决定禁止外国制造的机器人时，白宫提到了美国在机器人零部件和技术方面过度依赖外国供应商的威胁。 同样的依赖可能会为外国实体创造一种“在他们选择的时间扰乱或破坏供应链”的方式。 另一个担忧是，间谍活动可能会通过机器人的传感器进行。

美国联邦通信委员会表示：“鉴于这些证据，美国政府对国家安全有一个明确且令人信服的担忧，即外国生产的先进机器人设备可能被武器化，直接损害美国国家安全和美国人。”

经验

我当记者已经超过 15 年了。 我的职业生涯始于堪萨斯城的学校和城市记者，并于 2017 年加入 PCMag，负责报道卫星互联网服务、网络安全、PC 硬件等。 我目前居住在旧金山，但之前在中国工作了五年多，负责该国的技术行业。

自 2020 年以来，我报道了 SpaceX Starlink 卫星互联网服务的推出和爆炸性增长，撰写了 600 多个有关可用性和功能发布的故事，还报道了卫星星座扩张的监管之争、与 AST SpaceMobile 和亚马逊等竞争对手提供商的斗争，以及扩展到基于卫星的移动服务的努力。 我梳理了 FCC 文件以获取最新消息，并开车前往加利福尼亚州的偏远角落测试 Starlink 的蜂窝服务。

我还介绍了网络威胁，从勒索软件团伙到基于人工智能的恶意软件的出现。 正如我与 Motherboard 的联合调查所披露的，在 2024 年和 2025 年，FTC 迫使 Avast 向消费者支付 1650 万美元，因为该公司秘密收集消费者的个人信息并将其出售给第三方客户。

我还报道了 PC 显卡市场。 大流行时期的短缺导致我在百思买 (Best Buy) 前扎营购买了 RTX 3000。 我现在正在关注人工智能驱动的内存短缺如何影响整个消费电子市场。 我总是渴望了解更多信息，因此请在评论中提供反馈并向我发送提示。
